explanation:
According to Archimedes' Principle, the upthrust (or buoyant force) acting on a body immersed in a fluid is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the body. Since the problem states that the body displaces 12N of liquid, the upthrust is exactly 12N. The weight of the body (20N) is irrelevant to calculating the magnitude of the upthrust, though it indicates the body will sink because the upthrust is less than its weight.
